indicators.note: something trapped by the poles sits between them, so the verb goes inside the pair

parts.note: the two magnetic poles, south and north
to bear children is to have them

explanation.surface: A shaven bear held captive by Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal but is the verb, and 'Poles' are the compass ends, not Polish people.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaven head or chin has had its growth removed with a razor, leaving it bare.

clue.text: Ancient dictator upset the whole of America

indicators.note: in a down clue an upset word is turned upside down, so the phrase reads from the bottom up

parts.note: the whole of something is all of it
the US, United States

explanation.surface: A Roman tyrant who has offended an entire nation.
explanation.walkthrough: SULLA was the Roman general who made himself dictator in 82 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucius Cornelius Sulla seized power in Rome and ruled as dictator, a historical example.

clue.text: Nana perhaps starts to admire immense weapon

parts.note: British slang for a silly person, a fool, which is also an ass
eg, 'for example', marks Nana as just one instance

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words are their opening letters

parts.note: the first letters of admire and immense

explanation.surface: Granny might begin to admire a huge spear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nana' looks like a grandmother; here it is the British slang for a twit. An ASSEGAI is a slender iron-tipped spear used in southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The assegai is a throwing spear, a traditional arm of Zulu warriors.

indicators.note: the wrinkles are placed in the lugs, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: lug is British informal for an ear
lines on the face

explanation.surface: Wrinkled ears as a sign of ageing too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: Lugs is a British informal word for ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Being early is coming before the due time, which is what prematurity means.

indicators.note: letters that are manipulated have been handled and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the Dow Jones, the New York stock index

explanation.surface: Someone has fiddled with an index fund that tracks the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Index tracker' reads as a finance term, but the definition is only 'tracker'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shadow is someone who follows another person secretly, keeping track of their movements.

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the setter's paper, the Financial Times, speaking of itself

explanation.surface: A burly American man greets us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is the Financial Times, the paper the puzzle appears in.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone large, heavy and powerfully built.

indicators.note: the answer comes from within the run of letters across the two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of unbridled and the start of Rachmanism

explanation.surface: Profits made by unrestrained exploitative landlords.
explanation.walkthrough: Rachmanism is the exploitation of tenants by slum landlords, after Peter Rachman of 1950s London.
explanation.definitionFit: The drachma was the Greek currency until the euro replaced it in 2002.

indicators.note: an upset arrangement is knocked over and jumbled

parts.note: the nine letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sly sort who annoyed a lover of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weaselly' looks like a character insult, but it is literal: the animal is the largest of the weasel family.
explanation.definitionFit: The wolverine is a member of the mustelid family, which includes weasels.

indicators.note: without its end the word loses its final letter

parts.note: clot is British informal for a fool
sure of oneself

explanation.surface: Teasing a fool who is far too self-assured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winding up' suggests teasing, but here it means bringing to an end. A clot is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Closure is the act of bringing something to a finish, as in winding up a business.

clue.text: Easy to approach anonymous fellow with story

parts.note: A or anon. is the abbreviation for anonymous, as on an unsigned poem
a fable is a short moral tale

explanation.surface: An unnamed man with a tale to tell is friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: An affable person is pleasant and friendly, so others find them approachable.

clue.text: Stuffing turkey's opening with nutty ready-mix

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of turkey

indicators.note: nutty means crazy, so the letters go wild

parts.note: the eight letters of ready-mix are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Christmas recipe: stuffing the bird with a nutty packet mix.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about cooking stuffing, but the definition means stuffing dead animals for display.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxidermy is the craft of preparing and mounting animal skins, filling them so they look lifelike.

indicators.note: something mismanaged is badly handled, so the letters end up out of order

parts.note: the ten letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Students are furious because the university is badly run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' reads as a British swear word for emphasis; here it means involving bloodshed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguinary describes battles or people marked by much slaughter and bloodshed.

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: to heal is to recover

explanation.surface: A rumour that you will receive a better tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a gratuity, but here it is the verb used of a boat leaning over.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship heels when it leans to one side, which is to tilt or list.

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used, a run lying inside the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the end of delicious and into pineapples

explanation.surface: Putting tasty pineapple into jars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like a verb about preserving fruit; it is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both bottle and spine are informal words for nerve or courage.

clue.text: Right pig stalking celebrity on date

indicators.note: the pig follows behind the celebrity, so it comes after
in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a famous person is a star
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A boar following a famous person around on a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' is the adjective of direction: STARBOARD is the right-hand side of a ship looking forward.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, starboard is the side to the right as one faces the bow.

indicators.note: rattled things are shaken up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the eight letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bravery that gets flustered is unattractive.
explanation.walkthrough: INFRA DIG, short for Latin infra dignitatem, means beneath one's dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbecoming is unseemly, beneath one's dignity, which is what the Latin phrase says.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a body of fans or supporters

explanation.walkthrough: One word serves as an adjective meaning next and as a noun for a group of fans.
explanation.definitionFit: A following is a band of devoted supporters, while following also means coming next in time.

clue.text: Blind Jack, a villain without the first bit of integrity

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
taken as written

indicators.note: here without has its old sense of outside, so the villain goes around the letter

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person

indicators.note: the first bit of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of integrity

explanation.surface: A sightless sailor who is a scoundrel lacking any honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but it is the old sense of outside. A JALOUSIE is a slatted window blind.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalousie is a shutter or window covering of angled slats, a type of blind.

indicators.note: the cocaine is placed in the rearranged word
a busy scene is all bustle and confusion, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the six letters of bourse are rearranged
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: Concealing drugs on a crowded stock exchange floor.
explanation.walkthrough: A bourse is a stock exchange, especially in continental Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to conceal it from view, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Retired Poirot perhaps stripped for money

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the name is read in reverse
stripped of its outer layer, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Hercule Poirot, Agatha Christie's detective, is one bearer of the first name

explanation.surface: A retired detective who has been robbed of his savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poirot perhaps' points to his first name, not his surname; the definition tag marks it as one example of a Hercule.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, especially when gained dishonestly, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: Initially clean top half of legs beneath bum crease

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of clean

parts.note: first letter of clean

indicators.note: beneath means placed under, after the previous piece in this down entry

parts.note: rump is a word for the bottom, the bum

indicators.note: top half of keeps the first two of the four letters of legs

parts.note: the first half of legs

explanation.surface: Cleaning the upper legs below the bottom, ironing out a crease.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, beneath means coming later, so the half of legs follows the word for bum.
explanation.definitionFit: To crumple is to crush into wrinkles, so as a verb it matches crease.

clue.text: Oddly ignoring new baby, finally shrugs and goes out

indicators.note: ignoring the odd letters leaves the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: the even letters of new baby

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter

parts.note: the last letter of shrugs

explanation.surface: A parent indifferent to a newborn shrugs and leaves the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes out' sounds like leaving home; it is the tide receding.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide ebbs when it flows back out from the shore.

clue.text: Foolish ritual of silent central bank boss

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay quiet
the BoJ, Bank of Japan, is Japan's central bank
an umbo is the raised boss at the centre of a shield

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped central bank governor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central bank boss' looks like one title but splits into the Bank of Japan and a shield boss, the umbo.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbo jumbo is meaningless ceremony or superstitious ritual, nonsense dressed up as rite.

clue.text: Half-heartedly deal with disorder among animals

parts.note: to manage a task is to deal with it

explanation.surface: Dealing grudgingly with chaos in a zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorder' looks like chaos; it means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mange is a skin disease of dogs and other animals caused by parasitic mites.

parts.note: to boo is to jeer

parts.note: the first and last letters of rumbustious

explanation.surface: Mock the very rowdy louts.
explanation.definitionFit: Boors are rude, ill-mannered people, the same as clumsy louts.

NY, New York City

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man City' is the usual nickname of Manchester City; here the words split into a man's name and a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Calumny is the making of false statements that damage someone's reputation, i.e. defamation.

clue.text: Supporter of mine very softly embracing sex professional

indicators.note: the outer letters embrace, or hold, the inner pieces

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, the musical direction
it is a coy word for sex
a pro

indicators.note: the sea lies beyond, so comes after, the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
the Med, Mediterranean
